title: Schedule of Release Limits by the Age of the Cancelled Journey — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
# Air Ticket Fare Brands: Release Limits by the Age of the Cancelled Journey

Footnote to the travel credit lines of the Air Ticket Fare Brands tariff. How long ago the cancelled journey was due is counted in whole days from the outbound departure date to the handling date. The stale-journey term is 90 whole days. What the age of the journey settles is a share taken on the pool available to the traveller.

| Where the outbound departure date | The share taken on the pool available to the traveller |
| --- | --- |
| passed more than 90 whole days before the handling date | the pool available to the traveller is taken at 0.6 |
| has passed, but by not more than 90 whole days | the pool available to the traveller is taken at 0.85 |
| has not passed | the pool available to the traveller is taken in full |

Either side of the term: where the count comes to 90 whole days exactly, the departure date has passed by not more than the stale-journey term, and the pool available to the traveller is taken at 0.85; where the count comes to 91 whole days, the departure date passed more than that term ago, and that pool is taken at 0.6. On hypothetical dates, an outbound departure of 1 March handled on 30 May counts 90 whole days, so the pool available to the traveller is taken at 0.85; the same departure handled on 31 May counts 91 whole days, so that pool is taken at 0.6.

Where the itinerary is handled on the outbound departure date itself, the count is zero whole days: the date has passed by not more than 90 whole days, and the pool available to the traveller is taken at 0.85. Where the outbound departure date still lies ahead of the handling date, no such share is taken and that pool is taken in full.
